reason: Seeing the left-hand side cross y = 1 only once, and only for x > 0, shows why x = 6 is kept and x = -3 is rejected.

scenes.title: Why only x = 6 survives
scenes.purpose: See the left-hand side as a curve that only exists for x > 0, crossing y = 1 once, so the second quadratic root is not a solution.

steps.text: The power law gives $2\log_3 x = \log_3 x^2$, so the left side is $\log_3\frac{x^2}{x+6}$. Drag $k$ and watch $P$ move on this curve. This is the B1.
The equation asks for the left side to equal $1$, that is $\frac{x^2}{x+6} = 3$. Drag $k$ to $6$: $P$ meets the line $y=1$, and $36/12 = 3$. Combining first, then removing the logs, is the M1.

The quadratic $x^2-3x-18=0$ (dashed, scaled down) has roots $x=6$ and $x=-3$. But the log curve has no points at all for $x \leqslant 0$, since $\log_3(-3)$ is undefined. So $x=-3$ is rejected and $x=6$ only. This is the A1.

guide.what_you_see: The curve $y=2\log_3 x-\log_3(x+6)$, the left side of the equation, drawn only for $x>0$, with the horizontal line $y=1$ and the $y$-axis marked. A point $P$ on the curve shows the value of the left side at your chosen $x$.

legend.meaning: The curve $y=2\log_3 x-\log_3(x+6)=\log_3\frac{x^2}{x+6}$, the left-hand side of the equation. It has no points for $x\leqslant 0$.
A point on $L$ at $x=k$, set by the slider, whose height is the value of the left side at that $x$.
The dashed curve $y=\frac{x^2-3x-18}{6}$, the quadratic from the working scaled down by $6$. It crosses the $x$-axis at the roots $x=-3$ and $x=6$.
The point $(6,1)$, where $L$ meets the line $y=1$. It is the solution $x=6$.
The horizontal line $y=1$, the right-hand side of the equation.
The vertical line $x=0$ (the $y$-axis). The logarithms are only defined to its right.

interact.do: Drag the slider from $0.5$ up to $12$, stopping at $k=2$, then at $k=6$.
interact.watch: $P$ moves along $L$ and the reading updates. At $k=2$ the value is $\log_3\frac{4}{8}\approx -0.63$, below the line $y=1$. At $k=6$ it is $\log_3 3=1$ and $P$ sits on the line $y=1$ at $(6,1)$. For larger $k$ it rises above $1$, so $L$ crosses $y=1$ only once.

question_link.text: The curve $L$ is the combined left side $\log_3\frac{x^2}{x+6}$ from the power law (B1), and $P$ reaching height $1$ at $x=6$ is the equation $\frac{x^2}{x+6}=3$ from the M1 working. The dashed quadratic has a second root at $x=-3$, but $L$ has no points there, which is why that root is rejected for the A1.

read_off: The label 'At $x=k$ the left side is …' gives the value of $2\log_3 x-\log_3(x+6)$ at the slider's $x$-value. The solution is where this reads exactly $1$, which happens at $k=6$.
